title: A finite arithmetic form of Robin's inequality and its equivalence to the Riemann hypothesis
summary: Robin's inequality reformulates the Riemann hypothesis as a bound on the sum-of-divisors function $σ$. We introduce a finite-truncation version of Robin's inequality determined intrinsically by the arithmetic structure of $n$, \[ \frac{σ(n)}{n} 5040, \] where $ω(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$, and $γ$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. The resulting bound is pointwise stronger than Robin's inequality and we prove it unconditionally for integers with $ω(n)\le 6$, primorials, odd integers and square-free integers.
